title: 65_HS1-834228961_62-HQ-83894_Serial_220
what_is_it: A translated letter from a Mexican inventor to a U.S. scientific commission proposing theories about flying saucers, accompanied by a newspaper clipping about the first photographs of a 'flying saucer' taken in Durango, Mexico.
core_summary: Miguel Angel Garcia Macias, a self-described pianist, composer, and 'ideographic inventor' from Veracruz, Mexico, wrote to the President of the Commission of Scientific Investigation of the United States on March 19, 1950, sharing his theories about 'stratospheric aerostats' (flying saucers) and listing his various unpatented inventions. The letter was accompanied by a Mexican newspaper article reporting that engineering student German Horacio Robles Jr. took what were claimed to be the first photographs of a flying saucer over Durango at approximately 9,000 feet altitude, describing the object as a double truncated cone using jet-like propulsion.
interpretation_warnings: The letter writer Garcia Macias was a self-described 'ideographic inventor' with no apparent scientific credentials; his claims about velocities exceeding light are physically impossible and reflect a lack of scientific grounding.
The Durango photographs are described only via a newspaper clipping caption; no photographic analysis or verification by any agency is included in this document.
The newspaper clipping is from a Mexican publication (appears to be Excelsior), not an official investigative report — it is a media account, not a verified observation.
The document is a translation by Mrs. Sophia Saliba; the original Spanish text is also included but OCR quality is poor, making cross-verification difficult.
Garcia Macias believed flying saucers were U.S. atomic-powered craft, which was a common speculation in 1950 and is not supported by evidence.
This appears to be unsolicited correspondence received by the FBI, not an FBI investigation or assessment.

public_headline: Mexican Inventor Wrote FBI About Flying Saucer Theories in 1950
public_tldr: This FBI file contains a translated 1950 letter from a Mexican inventor named Miguel Angel Garcia Macias, who shared his personal theories about flying saucers with a U.S. scientific commission, along with a Mexican newspaper clipping reporting the first alleged photographs of a flying saucer over Durango, Mexico. The document is unsolicited correspondence — not an FBI investigation or assessment.
public_narrative:
In March 1950, a man named Miguel Angel Garcia Macias — a self-described pianist, composer, and "ideographic inventor" from Veracruz, Mexico — wrote a letter addressed to the "President of the Commission of Scientific Investigation of the United States." In it, he laid out his personal theories about what he called "stratospheric aerostats," his term for flying saucers. He believed the United States already possessed these craft and that they were powered by atomic force. He also claimed the devices could achieve velocities "greater than that of light or sound," a claim that has no basis in physics.

Garcia Macias used the letter to list several of his own unpatented inventions, including a "graduated dropper" and automatic shovels for dump trucks. He alleged that plans for some of these inventions had been stolen from him and patented by unknown persons in the United States. None of these claims were investigated or verified within this document.

Attached to the letter was a clipping from a Mexican newspaper dated March 16, 1950, reporting that an engineering student named German Horacio Robles Jr. had taken what were claimed to be the first photographs of a flying saucer over the city of Durango. The newspaper described the object as a "double truncated cone, joined at its bases," flying at an altitude of 8,000 to 9,000 feet and moving by something resembling jet propulsion.

The letter was translated into English by Mrs. Sophia Saliba and appears to have been received by the FBI's New York office. There is no indication in the file that the FBI conducted any follow-up investigation, analysis of the photographs, or assessment of Garcia Macias's claims. This is unsolicited mail that was filed, not an investigative report.
public_caveats: Garcia Macias had no apparent scientific credentials. His claim that flying saucers could exceed the speed of light reflects a fundamental misunderstanding of physics, not insider knowledge.
The Durango flying saucer photographs are described only through a newspaper clipping caption. No photographic analysis or verification by any official body is included in this document.
The newspaper source appears to be a Mexican publication (possibly Excelsior), meaning the flying saucer account is a media report — not a verified military or scientific observation.
This document is unsolicited correspondence received by the FBI, not an FBI investigation, assessment, or endorsement of any claims made within it.
The document was translated from Spanish by Mrs. Sophia Saliba; the original Spanish text is included but in poor condition, making independent cross-verification of the translation difficult.
